name: Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli
nameAr: يونس بن يزيد بن أبي النجاد الأيلي القرشي الأموي مولاهم

nisbas.en: al-Ayli, of Ayla on the Red Sea
al-Umawi (as a client of the Umayyads)

mawla: the family of Abu Sufyan; Tahdhib al-Tahdhib names Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan as his patron

orthography.spelled: al-Ayli: fatha on the hamza, the ya unvowelled, then lam (الأَيْلي).

diedNote: 159 AH on the sounder view; also said 160

taqrib.ar: ثقة إلا أن في روايته عن الزهري وهما قليلا وفي غير الزهري خطأ
taqrib.en: Reliable, except that there is a little error in his transmission from al-Zuhri, and mistakes in his transmission from others.

role: One of al-Zuhri's closest companions; al-Zuhri lodged with him at Ayla

verdicts.ar: نحن لا نقدم في الزهري على يونس أحدا، وكان الزهري إذا قدم أيلة نزل على يونس، وإذا سار إلى المدينة زامله يونس
verdicts.en: We put no one ahead of Yunus in al-Zuhri's hadith. When al-Zuhri came to Ayla he lodged with Yunus, and when he travelled to Madinah Yunus rode with him.

verdicts.ar: يونس أكثر حديثا عن الزهري من عقيل، وهما ثقتان
verdicts.en: Yunus has more hadith from al-Zuhri than Uqayl, and both are reliable.

verdicts.ar: في حديث يونس عن الزهري منكرات… وعقيل أقل خطأ منه
verdicts.en: There are objectionable things in Yunus's hadith from al-Zuhri; Uqayl makes fewer mistakes than he. Al-Athram adds that Ahmad faulted him for turning al-Zuhri's own opinions into reports from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, because the way he wrote his notes ran the two together.

verdicts.ar: كان ابن المبارك يقول: كتابه صحيح. قال ابن مهدي: وأنا أقول: كتابه صحيح
verdicts.en: Ibn al-Mubarak used to say his book is sound, and I too say his book is sound.

verdicts.ar: إني إذا نظرت في حديث معمر ويونس يعجبني كأنهما خرجا من مشكاة واحدة
verdicts.en: When I look at the hadith of Ma'mar and Yunus it delights me; it is as though they came out of a single lamp-niche.

flags.label: Strongest from his written copy
flags.detail: Ahmad's reservations concern reports Yunus gave from memory, where al-Zuhri's opinions and Sa'id's reports ran together in his notes; Ibn al-Mubarak and Ibn Mahdi vouched for his book. His transmission from al-Zuhri, when carried by Ibn Wahb and Ibn al-Mubarak as here, is the material the two Sahihs rely on.

bio: A client of the Umayyad house from the port of Ayla, where al-Zuhri would stay with him, and one of the most prolific transmitters of al-Zuhri's hadith. Ahmad ibn Salih would put no one ahead of him in al-Zuhri; Ahmad ibn Hanbel preferred Uqayl and Ma'mar for precision while still calling him reliable. He died in Upper Egypt in 159 AH. His kunya, Abu Yazid, matches his father's name, a pattern Ibn Hajar lists among the things a hadith student should notice.

provenance.ref: Shamela narrator record 7248, drawing on Tahdhib al-Kamal 32/551 and Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 4/474
al-Kashif 4/555, as quoted on the Shamela record
Chains of Sahih al-Bukhari 6, 71, 3116 and Sahih Muslim 1037
